content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to [product_name] and having difficulties setting up a daily schedule for my greenhouse. I have a [product_name] [article_no], the cable, and [product_name] [version_no]. My goal is to get sprinklers to start at 8am and run for 5 seconds, repeating every 30 minutes until 8pm. Could someone assist me with this? Best regards, [user_name]

Hello, You can utilize a Weekly Timer to trigger an asynchronous pulse generator. Set the pulse width to 5 seconds and the interval between pulses to 30 minutes. That should accomplish your goal. Regards,

Hi [user_name], Thank you for your prompt and helpful reply. I have an additional question: How can I schedule the sprinklers at different times? For example: - From 8am to 11am, run for 5 seconds every 30 minutes. - From 11am to 4pm, run for 10 seconds every 20 minutes (since greenhouse temperature varies throughout the day, I need longer intervals at midday). - From 4pm to 8pm, run for 5 seconds every 30 minutes. Based on your previous advice, I tried using multiple Weekly Timers and asynchronous pulse generators linked to the same output, but it didn’t work. Regards, [user_name]
Hello, If you connect the outputs of the various asynchronous timers using an OR block to the output, it should function correctly. Regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], Thanks again for your quick reply. I implemented your suggestion and made the logic more complex: the operating duration now increases during the day and decreases in the evening, which matches the temperature fluctuations. It appears to be working well in the simulation. I attached an image of the circuit. Regards, [user_name]
Hello, If the system works for your needs, that's great. I would suggest including a temperature measurement to further optimize the watering based on conditions. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are configuring a greenhouse sprinkler system using [product_name] software and module. The challenge is setting up multiple schedules with varying intervals and durations depending on the time of day. Initial simple timer logic did not meet requirements, leading to more advanced logical wiring and testing in simulation. Manual iteration and combining logical blocks were necessary to achieve the desired schedule.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to easily design and adjust dynamic daily schedules in [product_name] software and for the logic to run reliably on the associated hardware module.
